chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Muhrim (person in Ihram) does not point out the game; if he points it out and it is killed, then upon him is the redemption (kaffarah).

key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: Redemption or compensation (usually involving sacrificing an animal or feeding the poor)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (sacred consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person in Ihram points out game and it gets killed?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between mere indication (dalal) and active hunting, establishing that accidental pointing incurs fidyah rather than the heavier penalty for deliberate hunting. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on intent and the specific conditions under which a pilgrim’s minor actions trigger compensation, ensuring the sanctity of the Haram is maintained without undue harshness.
